After You Make a Mistake at Work

Open this in the hour after you realize you got something wrong at work, when your stomach has dropped and you want to hide. It helps you tell the right person, fix what can be fixed, and stop the replay from taking over your week.

Mistakes · Work · Shame · Self-Compassion · 8 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Write down what happened in plain order — Facts on paper are smaller and clearer than the version in your head.
  • Tell the person who needs to know first — Bad news travels better from you than from someone else.
  • Say what you are doing about it — A mistake plus a plan is a very different conversation.
  • Repair the part that can still be repaired — Acting on the fixable piece takes the helpless feeling out of it.
  • Keep the error apart from your worth — You did something wrong, which is not the same as being no good at this.
  • Note the one step that would have caught it — A single check added is worth more than an hour of self-blame.
  • Set a time to stop thinking about it — A limit on the replay keeps one afternoon from becoming a week.
  • Tell someone outside work how it felt — Saying it out loud to a friend takes the shame out of the room.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
